facts.text: On this date in 1945, the United Nations officially came into existence — yet its founding document, the UN Charter, had already been signed four months earlier in San Francisco by nations that included countries still under colonial rule.

On this date in 1648, the Peace of Westphalia ended the Thirty Years War and invented the modern concept of national sovereignty — a diplomatic idea now so foundational that it shapes every border dispute on Earth.
Manila is the world's most densely populated city proper, packing over 111,000 people per square kilometer — nearly double the density of Dhaka and more than ten times that of New York City.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka with a 1,000 km radius than in the entire Western Hemisphere.

Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined, holding roughly 60% of the world's fresh surface water in lake form — yet two-thirds of Canadian municipalities rely on groundwater for drinking.

On this date in 1929, the New York Stock Exchange suffered 'Black Thursday' — 12.9 million shares traded in a single day of panic, nearly triple the norm, triggering the crash that erased $30 billion in market value within weeks.

On October 24, 1857, every bank in the United States suspended specie payments simultaneously — the first truly national financial panic, caused largely by collapsing railroad speculation and a single failed Ohio bank.
The S&P 500 has historically risen in the six months following a U.S. midterm election every single time since 1950 — a streak so consistent it has its own name among analysts: the midterm miracle.
Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway holds more U.S. Treasury bills than the Federal Reserve itself — over $300 billion in cash equivalents as of 2025, a sum larger than the GDP of Portugal.

The Dutch East India Company, history's first publicly traded corporation, was so dominant at its peak that it employed 50,000 people, maintained a private army, and its inflation-adjusted market cap exceeded $8 trillion.

On this date in 1946, a camera aboard a captured V-2 rocket took the first photograph of Earth from space — a grainy black-and-white image shot from 65 miles up, changing forever how humanity pictured its home.
Your skeleton is not the rigid scaffold it appears. Bone is living tissue that completely replaces itself every decade, and it responds to mechanical stress by growing denser, like a muscle.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.

On this date in 1929, the stock market began its historic collapse — but the shockwave traveled at the speed of human panic, not light. Modern financial contagion can now circle the globe in 40 milliseconds via fiber optic cables.
The human eye can detect a single photon in absolute darkness. Your visual system is not limited by biology — it is limited by the quantum nature of light itself.
On this day in 1945, the United Nations officially came into existence — younger than many people alive today, and younger than the Slinky, which launched the previous week.
The fax machine was patented in 1843, twenty-three years before the first transatlantic telegraph cable worked reliably. You could fax before you could reliably wire-telegraph across an ocean.
On this day in 1929, Black Thursday opened on Wall Street. The traders who caused the crash were, on average, younger than the S&P 500 index is now.
Oxford University was already three centuries old when the Aztec Empire was founded. It was teaching students before Tenochtitlán was a blueprint.
Nintendo was incorporated in 1889, making it older than commercial air travel, the zipper, and the nation of Finland — it started as a playing card company and outlasted empires.
Meraki (μεράκι): Greek for doing something with soul, creativity, and love — leaving a piece of yourself in your work. There is no clean English equivalent, which says something about English.
Hiraeth: Welsh longing for a home you cannot return to, or never had. It folds grief, nostalgia, and belonging into a single breath that English needs an entire paragraph to approximate.
On this date in 1648, the Peace of Westphalia was signed — and the word 'sovereignty' entered the political lexicon as a practical reality, not just a philosophical one.
Sonder: coined in 2012 by John Koenig, the realization that every passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Its youth does not make it less necessary.
Vellichor: also Koenig's invention, the strange wistfulness of used bookshops — places haunted by the lives of readers who never finished what they started.
On this date in 2021, Bitcoin hit an all-time high above $66,000 — then lost half its value within weeks. The rally was partly driven by the ProShares futures ETF launch, not spot demand.
On Oct 24, 2008, Satoshi Nakamoto sent the Bitcoin whitepaper to a cryptography mailing list. Nine people replied. None thought it would work.
The Ethereum 'Merge' in Sept 2022 cut the network's energy use by ~99.95%. It also made every pre-merge ETH miner's hardware instantly worthless overnight.
Bitcoin's smallest unit, the satoshi, is 0.00000001 BTC. At peak 2021 prices, one sat was worth roughly $0.00066 — yet Lightning Network routes payments at this precision in milliseconds.

The DAO hack in 2016 drained 3.6M ETH through a reentrancy bug. The attacker moved slowly enough that the community hard-forked Ethereum before the funds fully cleared — creating ETH and ETC in one exploit.

On this date in 2015, Google open-sourced TensorFlow. Within two years it became the most-starred ML repo on GitHub, accelerating the shift from proprietary internal tools to shared infrastructure across the entire field.

On this date in 2022, a preprint revealed that GPT-3's training data contained benchmark test sets verbatim, meaning years of reported SOTA scores were partly measuring memorization, not generalization.

AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins — essentially the entire known proteome — in roughly 18 months. The same task would have taken classical crystallography longer than the age of the universe.

The transformer architecture, now the backbone of nearly every frontier model, was proposed in a 2017 paper whose working title was 'Attention Is All You Need' — a phrase its authors considered too glib to keep, then kept anyway.
Training GPT-4 is estimated to have consumed more compute than the combined total of all ML experiments published in every academic venue from 1950 to 2010. The scaling cliff hasn't appeared yet.
